newsitem.title: USA: Massachusetts to raise pension funding - report.
newsitem.headline: Massachusetts to raise pension funding - report.

text.p: The Massachusetts House of Representatives budget to be unveiled next week is expected to contain a provision to pay off ahead of schedule a huge gap in the state's pension funds, State House News Service reported.

The unfunded liability stands at $6.7 billion, down from $17 billion 10 years ago, House Ways and Means Committee Chairman Paul Haley, D-Weymouth, said. The goal is to eliminate the unfunded liability by the year 2018, 10 years earlier than scheduled under terms of a law passed in the 1980s.
"A tremendous return on investments and solid management" of the system account for the improved numbers during recent years, Haley said.

But he and others said it would imprudent, after all the progress that has been made, to retain the 30-year schedule, as recommended by state Treasurer Joseph Malone, and make $2 billion available to help pay for the Central Artery/Third Harbor Tunnel project.
Massachusetts general obligation debt is currently rated A-plus by Standard & Poor's Corp; A1 by Moody's Investors Service and A-plus by Fitch Investors Service, which has it on a positive trend.

State law requires that the administration propose, and the House Ways and Means Committee approve, a new funding schedule every three years. The revised schedule is being acted on a year earlier than required.

The fiscal 1998 budget Haley will release next week will recommend appropriating $1.045 billion for the state's pension fund, $92.7 million more than Gov. William Weld recommended in his budget proposal in January, the report said.
